candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13 / PDF p.17
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize common liver/biliary and bone sources of elevated alkaline phosphatase.

options.A: Hepatobiliary and bone sources are common possibilities, and additional evaluation may be needed to identify the source
options.B: An elevated ALP can only originate from kidney disease
options.C: An elevated ALP always identifies one specific bone disorder
options.D: ALP has no relationship to hepatobiliary or skeletal conditions

candidate.rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories states that serum ALP is used in evaluation of hepatobiliary disease and bone disease associated with increased osteoblastic activity. ALP isoenzyme testing can help distinguish liver from bone sources. Therefore, an elevated ALP is not specific to a single organ or diagnosis.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Supports liver and bone as important sources of elevated ALP and use of isoenzymes to help localize the source.
candidate.source_document_title: Alkaline Phosphatase, Total and Isoenzymes, Serum (ALKP)
candidate.stem: An adult has a markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP). Which interpretation is most appropriate?
